title: Sig Fig Sleuth: Significant Figures — ItsDrDan
author: Dr. Dan (ItsDrDan)

chapters.CHEM 3A: Chapter 1: Basics of Measurement (1.1 Scientific Notation, 1.2 Significant Figures)
chapters.CHEM 1A: Chapter 1.5: Measurement Uncertainty, Accuracy, and Precision (OpenStax)

description: Significant figures practice for CHEM 3A Chapter 1 (default) and CHEM 1A Chapter 1.5 (add ?course=1A). Students pick from 4 main options, Counting Sig Figs, Rounding, Sig Figs in Math, and Lab Measurements, then turn individual topics on or off and can mix several at once: count sig figs, spot the sig figs (tap the digits), exact vs measured, round to sig figs, decimal places, scientific notation, × and ÷, + and −, multi-step (round at the end), read the glassware, read digital equipment, accuracy vs precision, and name that equipment (the 20 items on the CHEM 3A lab manual's Equipment List, by picture and by use). Lab readings use full pictures of real equipment with a zoomed-in view: ruler, 10/50/100 mL graduated cylinders, 50 mL buret (numbers increase downward), thermometer, beaker, volumetric pipets and flasks (two decimal places, like 10.00 mL), buret volume delivered (final − initial), volume by displacement, an analytical balance reading to 0.0001 g, digital thermometer, stopwatch, and mass by difference. Matched to the FCC CHEM 3A lab manual's recording rules. Accuracy vs precision uses dartboards and lab data with all four answers: both, precise only, accurate only, neither. Skill Check Prep: 10 questions focused on lab readings, then a study plan. Grading checks value and precision with mistake-specific feedback, step-by-step help, hints, a rules sheet, TI-36X Pro tips, XP, ranks, 10 achievements, and ItsDrDan videos that jump to the right moment.
